english.notes:
(i) These regulations apply to persons driving a bus on or after 10th September 2008 or driving a lorry on or after 10th September 2009.
(ii) "Relevant vehicle" means a vehicle for which is required a driving licence of category C, C+E, D or D+E as defined in Article 3(1) of the Driving Licences Directive, or a driving licence recognised as equivalent.
(iii) See regulation 3(2) for vehicles to which these regulations DO NOT apply.
(iv) In England, Wales and Northern Ireland, "forges" means makes a false document in order that it may be used as genuine.
(v) See regulation 13(5), (6), (7) and (8) for details in relation to the time limits on prosecutions.
(vi) See regulation 14 for the power to seize documents.
(vii) This offence applies from the 3rd December 2024 due to changes made by SI 2024/1160 to the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007. For the offences applying before this date, see H20125 (authority / qualification card / community licence certificate) and H21544 (Swiss CPC etc).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit on prosecutions:
Complex - see regulation 13 of the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
